text:
maya: quick question about routing precedence — we have two rules that both could match /api/v1/generate: one is path+header (enterprise) pinned to chat-prodigy v2.3, the other is path-only fallback pinned to latest-quant. which should actually win at runtime?

kevin: can you paste the rules? iirc we evaluate rule priority then specificity but there's been edge cases.

maya: here are simplified rules (pseudo-yaml):
```
routes:
  - name: generate-enterprise
    match:
      path_prefix: /api/v1/generate
      headers:
        x-tenant-tier: enterprise
    model_alias: chat-prodigy
    pin: v2.3
    priority: 10
  - name: generate-default
    match:
      path_prefix: /api/v1/generate
    model_alias: chat-prodigy
    pin: latest-quant
    priority: 5
```

andre: if we use numeric priority it's straightforward — higher wins. but we currently fall back to "first matching rule" in the router, which depends on evaluation order (not great).

samir: also worth noting header match is technically more specific, but our matchers don't compute specificity score today. i ran into this when tenant proxies set the header at ingress and a CDN stripped it — then the path-only rule won and customer got the wrong model.

kevin: hmm. two things: make rule evaluation deterministic (priority + specificity tie-break), and surface which condition matched in telemetry + console so SREs can debug.

maya: agreed. proposal: evaluation order = explicit priority field (higher first) -> specificity score (number of match clauses matched, headers>query>path) -> creation_time for deterministic tie-break. update telemetry: tag every request with matched_rule_id, matched_clause_set, alias_resolved_to (model id + version), and fallback_reason if any.

andre: +1 on telemetry fields. also add a small routing metrics set: rule_match_count, fallback_count, pin_mismatch_count, avg_latency_by_rule. that will let us detect "unexpected fallback" spikes.

samir: for rollout UX we should show rollouts per-alias with a little waterfall: incoming traffic %, rules contributing to traffic, and their match conditions. otherwise PMs can't reason about why a canary is not getting traffic.

kevin: implementation notes:
- router: accept priority (int) optional. default 0.
- compute specificity = count(headers)*3 + count(query)*2 + count(path)*1 (weights TBD).
- evaluation: sort by priority desc, then specificity desc, then creation_ts asc.
- ensure match engine short-circuits only after selecting winner (no "first match" race).

maya: that weighting looks fine as a starting point. unit tests needed: overlapping-header+path, header-missing->fallback, header-present-old-version-pin->fallback-to-compat, and CDN-stripped-header simulation.

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: created follow-up ticket #INF-892 (route-eval-determinism + telemetry tags) by maya.

andre: small UX ask — in Console when you inspect a route we should show the exact matching predicate that was evaluated, not just the human rule. e.g. "path_prefix=/api/v1/generate && header[x-tenant-tier]=enterprise". That will make postmortems much faster.

maya: i'll update the RFC draft and add the telemetry fields. samir can you own the console change? kevin + andre pair on router impl & tests?

samir: yep i'll take the console task, will add a per-request debug drawer to show matched_rule_id and alias resolution chain.

kevin: i'll open a PR for ordering + specificity math, and add a compatibility check to ensure pin exists in alias catalog before finalizing match.

andre: one more operational thing — when a rule pins a version that is incompatible with the customer's region/hardware, router should mark it as "incompatible_pin" and skip it (emit telemetry). prevents silent user-facing degradations.

maya: nice catch. add incompatible_pin to fallback_reason enumerations.

kevin: ack. timeline? can we get an MVP in 2 weeks (router + basic telemetry + tests) and console follow-up in the sprint after?

maya: sounds reasonable. i'll sync with PM and add to the roadmap. thanks everyone. :pray:

samir: quick note — also track per-tenant rule overrides in telemetry (tenant_override=true) so we can tell when a customer is forcing something.

andre: agreed. putting that in the ticket.

maya: closing loop — i'll post updates in this thread as PRs land.

kevin: :thumbsup:
